input_signals.name: Weakest-Link Self-Funded Innovation
input_signals.hypothesis: A research program is only durable if the firm can fund it in its *worst* cash-flow year, so the priced characteristic is the binding constraint — the lower of intangible commitment and downside cash-flow capacity — rather than the sum of two independently attractive traits.
input_signals.reasoning: MIN is non-separable: once one leg binds, improvements in the other add nothing, so the score cannot be produced by either published anomaly alone the way a rank product or double sort can. The quality leg is deliberately the five-year *floor* of operating cash flow to assets, a downside-persistence construct distinct from the level of cash profitability, which is exactly what determines whether R&D survives a bad state.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ), at ) ), ind_rank( ts_min( ratio( oancf, at ), 5 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Retained-Earnings-Financed Research Gate
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), SUB(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(re, ADD(dltt, dlc)), at)), 0.5))
input_signals.hypothesis: The same level of R&D capital is an asset when it sits on a balance sheet of accumulated retained earnings exceeding total debt, and a liability when it is carried by a debt-dependent firm that may be forced to cut research; the return sign on intangible intensity should flip across financing states.
input_signals.reasoning: The gate (re minus total debt, scaled by assets) is defined for every firm including debt-free innovators, who now receive the strongest positive weight instead of being dropped by a zero denominator. Replacing the arbitrary 0.5 coverage cut with a continuous industry rank centered at zero removes the knife-edge threshold while preserving a genuine sign flip: long self-financed heavy researchers, short debt-carried heavy researchers, near-neutral for low-R&D firms where the mechanism does not apply.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ), at ) ), sub( ind_rank( ratio( sub( re, add( dltt, dlc ) ), at ) ), 0.5 ) )

input_signals.name: Externally Financed Intangible Build
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), COALESCE(intan, 0)), 1), at)), IND_RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), at), NEG(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Intangible assets are poor collateral and generate no immediate cash, so a balance-sheet intangible build financed by new debt at a firm with weak internal cash generation is a fragile, forced-writedown-prone expansion, whereas the identical build funded from internal cash is not.
input_signals.reasoning: The conditioning leg is now the *financing source* of the expansion — new borrowing combined with low internal operating cash flow — rather than accruals or earnings volatility, so the signal tests funding fragility rather than rediscovering the accrual or earnings-quality anomalies. The negative slope should be concentrated in the subset with both high intangible build and high external-financing dependence, a joint condition neither leverage growth nor goodwill growth identifies alone.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( delta( add( coalesce( gdwl, 0 ), coalesce( intan, 0 ) ), 1 ), at ) ), ind_rank( sumrank( ratio( delta( add( dltt, dlc ), 1 ), at ), neg( ma( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Intangible Intensity with Margin Floor
input_signals.hypothesis: What makes intangible spending durable is not cash on hand but pricing power: firms whose worst-year net margin never collapses have moats that let R&D and brand outlays compound, whereas equally intensive spenders with a collapsing margin floor are subsidizing competitive erosion.
input_signals.reasoning: This keeps the successful weakest-link operator but swaps the quality channel from a balance-sheet/cash-flow floor to a downside *margin* floor, so it tests whether the gen-0 result reflects funding capacity or product-market durability. Scaling intangible spend by revenue rather than assets aligns both legs on the income statement, making the conjunction a statement about unit economics rather than about firm size or asset composition.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), revt ) ), ind_rank( ts_min( ratio( ib, revt ), 5 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Knowledge Share of Capital Renewal
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), ADD(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), dp))), IND_RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(oancf, at), 5)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms that direct a large share of total capital renewal toward knowledge and brand rather than physical depreciation replacement are building higher-return capital, but only when a cash-flow floor guarantees the renewal program will not be interrupted.
input_signals.reasoning: The intangibles leg is a bounded [0,1] composition measure — intangible outlays as a share of intangible outlays plus depreciation — which is scale-free, defined for essentially all firms with dp, and distinct from the R&D-to-assets intensity anomaly because it compares intangible against tangible capital consumption rather than against firm size. Pairing it with the cash-flow floor under MIN keeps the validated conjunction structure while testing a different intangibles construct and materially improving expected coverage.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), add( add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), coalesce( xad, 0 ) ), dp ) ) ), ind_rank( ts_min( ratio( oancf, at ), 5 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Never-Cut Research with Cash-Flow Drawdown Guard
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 5)), IND_RANK(SUB(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3), TS_MAX(RATIO(oancf, at), 5))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Durability is revealed by floors and drawdowns, not levels: a firm whose research intensity never fell below a high threshold in five years has an institutionalized program, and one whose current cash flow sits close to its own five-year peak has not entered the deterioration phase in which such programs get cut.
input_signals.reasoning: Both legs are new constructs rather than horizon rescalings of the archive: the intangibles leg is the minimum research intensity (commitment floor) instead of the cumulated R&D level, and the quality leg is the firm's cash-flow drawdown from its own historical peak instead of a cross-sectional cash-flow level or floor. The drawdown is a within-firm, self-referential measure, so it is close to orthogonal to profitability rankings and tests whether the gen-0 alpha comes from being profitable or from not deteriorating.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ts_min( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), at ), 5 ) ), ind_rank( sub( ma( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ), ts_max( ratio( oancf, at ), 5 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Funding Source of Material Intangible Builds
input_signals.expression: MUL(INDICATOR(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), COALESCE(intan, 0)), 1), at), 0.01), SUB(IND_RANK(SUB(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3), RATIO(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), at))), 0.5))
input_signals.hypothesis: Among firms actually expanding their booked intangible base by a material amount, the cross-section of subsequent returns is determined by whether that expansion was paid for out of operating cash flow or out of new borrowing; firms with no material build carry no information from this channel at all.
input_signals.reasoning: The indicator restricts the signal to genuine builders (intangible plus goodwill increase exceeding 1% of assets), which repairs the flagged inconsistency where uncentered ranking placed intangible *shrinkers*, not non-builders, at the neutral end. Within that conditioned population the score is a centered rank of internal cash flow minus new debt issuance, so the extreme deciles are internally funded versus debt-funded builders and everyone else is exactly zero — a clean state-dependence test rather than a sign flip of the archived signal.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( indicator( ratio( delta( add( coalesce( gdwl, 0 ), coalesce( intan, 0 ) ), 1 ), at ), 0.01 ), sub( ind_rank( sub( ma( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ), ratio( delta( add( dltt, dlc ), 1 ), at ) ) ), 0.5 ) )

input_signals.name: Cash Yield on Knowledge Capital
input_signals.hypothesis: Among firms that have actually built a material knowledge stock, the priced characteristic is how much operating cash flow that stock throws off per dollar invested; high-yield research franchises are underpriced relative to research programs that consume capital without converting it into cash.
input_signals.reasoning: The archive shows funding-capacity conjunctions work but has not yet tested intangible *yield* successfully — the gen-0 trend version failed mainly because the yield was measured as a five-year slope on a degenerate denominator. Here the materiality indicator (R&D capital above 5% of assets) removes the small-R&D firms whose yield explodes, and the centered rank makes the extreme deciles high-yield versus low-yield researchers rather than researchers versus non-researchers, which is the structure that delivered fmb 4.45 in gen 1.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( indicator( ratio( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ), at ), 0.05 ), sub( ind_rank( ratio( ma( oancf, 3 ), ts_sum( xrd, 5 ) ) ), 0.5 ) )

input_signals.name: Organic Minus Acquired Intangible Capital
input_signals.hypothesis: Not all intangible capital is equal: internally developed knowledge is expensed and unrecognized, while purchased goodwill is capitalized at deal prices that embed acquirer overpayment, so the organic-minus-acquired tilt of a firm's intangible base predicts returns once a cash-flow floor confirms the firm can sustain it.
input_signals.reasoning: Every archived intangibles leg so far measures intensity or composition versus tangible capital; none contrasts self-generated against purchased intangibles, which is where the accounting mispricing is concentrated. Netting five-year R&D against booked goodwill plus other intangibles produces one signed intangible-quality variable, and conjoining it with the validated worst-year cash-flow floor isolates firms whose unrecognized knowledge base is both large and financially supported.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( sub( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ), add( coalesce( gdwl, 0 ), coalesce( intan, 0 ) ) ), at ) ), ind_rank( ts_min( ratio( oancf, at ), 5 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Acquired-Intangible-Light Cash Floor
input_signals.hypothesis: The pricing content of the organic-minus-acquired construct may come entirely from its short side: firms carrying little purchased goodwill or booked intangibles while sustaining a cash-flow floor have not bought their growth, and this alone may be the durable-quality characteristic.
input_signals.reasoning: The gen-2 leader (fmb 5.08, alpha 4.9%) netted cumulative R&D against booked intangibles, but we cannot tell whether the R&D leg or the goodwill penalty drives it; this drops the R&D term while holding the cash-flow floor fixed, giving a clean decomposition against the archived Weakest-Link signal, which holds R&D and drops the goodwill penalty. If this matches the leader, the mechanism is acquisitiveness aversion rather than intangible productivity, which would redirect the remaining generations.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( neg( ratio( add( coalesce( gdwl, 0 ), coalesce( intan, 0 ) ), at ) ) ), ind_rank( ts_min( ratio( oancf, at ), 5 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Loss-Free Research Record
input_signals.hypothesis: What makes a research program credible is the *frequency* with which the firm earns a profit, not the magnitude of its cash-flow floor: a researcher that has been profitable in every one of the last five years has proven it can run its program without external rescue, while an equally research-intensive firm with recurring loss years is financing knowledge with other people's capital.
input_signals.reasoning: Every archived quality leg is a magnitude statistic (worst-year level, margin level, working capital level); a count of profitable years is a distinct, outlier-robust persistence statistic that separates the profitable-innovator population from the perennial-loss research population, which magnitude floors blur. It also produces a large, stable top group — most mature firms tie at five of five — so the long leg is determined by research intensity among consistently profitable firms, which should improve portfolio turnover and stability relative to the leader.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ), at ) ), ind_rank( ts_sum( indicator( ib, 0 ), 5 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Moat-Persistence Floor on Research Capital
input_signals.hypothesis: Durable intangible productivity is a competitive-advantage concept: the relevant condition is that the firm out-earned its industry peers even in its worst year, since an absolute cash-flow floor mostly reflects which industry the firm operates in rather than whether its knowledge capital confers an advantage.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the brand-capital test — which the critic correctly identified as confounded by advertising-disclosure selection — with a test of whether the archive's repeated cash-floor result is a moat effect or an industry-composition effect, taking the worst-year value of *industry-demeaned* cash-flow-to-assets. If alpha and the Fama-MacBeth slope hold or improve, the mechanism is firm-specific durable advantage supporting research, which is the economic story we are asked to identify; if they weaken, the archive's floors have been proxying for stable-industry membership.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ), at ) ), ind_rank( ts_min( ind_adj( ratio( oancf, at ) ), 5 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Joint-Failure Quadrant of Purchased Intangibles
input_signals.hypothesis: Purchased intangibles are dangerous only when they are not backed by cash generation: a firm can be safe either by carrying little goodwill or by generating a solid cash-flow floor, and the return penalty is concentrated in the single quadrant where both conditions fail.
input_signals.reasoning: The disjunctive MAX supplies exactly the contrast the critic said was missing — the score is computed on the whole cross-section, so goodwill-heavy firms with strong floors and goodwill-light firms with weak floors both sit high, and only the joint-failure group is isolated in the short leg, which no additive, multiplicative or subsample construction in the archive can produce. It is the logical complement of the accepted MIN version on the same two legs, so the pair jointly identifies whether the effect is a complementarity on the long side or an impairment-cliff penalty on the short side.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: max( ind_rank( neg( ratio( add( coalesce( gdwl, 0 ), coalesce( intan, 0 ) ), at ) ) ), ind_rank( ts_min( ratio( oancf, at ), 5 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Patient-Capital Research Commitment
input_signals.hypothesis: Research pays off over many years, so the financing that supports it must be long-dated: an intangible-intensive firm with a heavy short-term debt load faces rollover risk that forces mid-project cuts, while the same firm financed with equity or long-term debt can see the program through.
input_signals.reasoning: The archive has tested funding *level* (cash-flow floor), funding *stock* (working capital, retained earnings less debt) and total leverage, but never the *maturity* of the claims, which is the dimension most directly mismatched with a research program's payoff horizon. Short-term debt to assets is available for essentially all firms, so this also delivers a high-coverage test of whether the enabling condition is duration matching rather than solvency.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ), at ) ), ind_rank( neg( ratio( dlc, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Deal Premium Versus Identifiable Intangibles
input_signals.hypothesis: Booked intangibles are not one thing: identifiable intangibles (patents, licences, developed technology, customer lists) are asset-specific and separately saleable, whereas goodwill is the residual overpayment in a deal, so the market's penalty on intangible-heavy balance sheets should fall on the deal premium and not on identifiable intangible assets.
input_signals.reasoning: Every archived intangibles leg has lumped gdwl and intan into a single penalty term, so we have never learned which component carries the information; here the two are separated and netted on a common measurement basis (both are book values, avoiding the expensed-versus-capitalized mixing the critic flagged earlier), rewarding identifiable intangibles and double-penalising goodwill. Paired with the unchanged cash-flow floor, a strong result would say the durable-intangible story is about avoiding overpayment rather than avoiding capitalised intangibles per se, which changes what the final consolidated signal should contain.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( sub( sub( coalesce( intan, 0 ), coalesce( gdwl, 0 ) ), coalesce( gdwl, 0 ) ), at ) ), ind_rank( ts_min( ratio( oancf, at ), 5 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash-Flow Stability Rather Than Level Behind Intangible-Light Balance Sheets
input_signals.hypothesis: The mandated economic story is that intangible credibility comes from *stable* cash flows; if that is literally true, the second moment of cash-flow-to-assets should validate intangible-light balance sheets as well as or better than a level floor, because stability identifies predictable franchises rather than merely profitable ones.
input_signals.reasoning: Every archived quality leg is a first-moment statistic — worst-year level, mean level, industry-adjusted level, loss counts — so cash-flow volatility has never been isolated as a conditioning channel, and the one gen-0 attempt buried it inside an additive SUMRANK that failed for unrelated reasons. Because low volatility and high level are only moderately correlated, this discriminates a risk-stability mechanism from a profitability mechanism, which is a substantive economic distinction rather than a window ablation.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( neg( ratio( add( coalesce( gdwl, 0 ), coalesce( intan, 0 ) ), at ) ) ), ind_rank( neg( vol( ratio( oancf, at ), 5 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Research Capital Per Dollar of Capital Employed Including Deal Premium
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), ADD(at, ADD(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), COALESCE(intan, 0))))), IND_RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(oancf, at), 5)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Organic research intensity should be measured against the full capital the firm has deployed, with purchased intangibles counted twice because a dollar of goodwill represents capital consumed with no operating substance; a firm scores high only when its self-built knowledge stock is large relative to a capital base that is penalised for acquisitiveness.
input_signals.reasoning: The previous version divided by assets *less* intangibles, which — as the critic correctly noted — inverted the intended sign by rewarding goodwill-heavy firms; adding purchased intangibles to the denominator instead makes goodwill dilute the score, matching the archived organic-minus-acquired evidence. This gives a single scale-free ratio in which the two intangible channels interact multiplicatively rather than additively, so it tests whether the leader's dollar difference or a properly signed ratio is the better functional form before we consolidate.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ), add( at, add( coalesce( gdwl, 0 ), coalesce( intan, 0 ) ) ) ) ), ind_rank( ts_min( ratio( oancf, at ), 5 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Worst-Year Coverage of Near-Term Claims
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), COALESCE(intan, 0)), at))), IND_RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(oancf, ADD(dlc, lct)), 5)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The enabling condition for intangible-light durability is not the level of cash flow relative to assets but whether the worst year's cash flow still covered the claims falling due within the year, which is the constraint that actually forces asset sales and program cuts.
input_signals.reasoning: Every archived floor scales cash flow by assets, which conflates funding capacity with asset intensity; scaling by short-term debt plus current liabilities makes the floor a genuine coverage ratio in which numerator and denominator are both claims-on-cash concepts. This is a single new quality construct rather than a stack of two archived legs, and it tests whether the repeated cash-floor result is about profitability or about liquidity risk.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( neg( ratio( add( coalesce( gdwl, 0 ), coalesce( intan, 0 ) ), at ) ) ), ind_rank( ts_min( ratio( oancf, add( dlc, lct ) ), 5 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Research Backed by Cash Unit Economics
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(SUB(SUB(revt, cogs), dp), revt), 3)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Research is credible when the product it supports earns a wide margin after both cash production costs and capital consumption, since that margin — not the balance sheet — is what funds the next research cycle out of operations.
input_signals.reasoning: The archived margin test used net margin (ib/revt), which is mechanically depressed for research-intensive firms because R&D is expensed below the gross line, biasing the conjunction against exactly the firms the hypothesis targets; measuring margin after cogs and depreciation but before R&D removes that accounting bias. This isolates a product-market channel from the funding-capacity channel at coverage around 0.14, far above the leader's 0.091.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ), at ) ), ind_rank( ma( ratio( sub( sub( revt, cogs ), dp ), revt ), 3 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash Return on Acquisitiveness-Penalized Capital
input_signals.hypothesis: The right profitability denominator for an intangible-heavy firm counts purchased intangibles twice, because a dollar of goodwill is capital the firm actually paid out with no operating substance behind it; cash flow measured against that penalised capital base is the return the acquirer really earned.
input_signals.reasoning: Rather than subtracting volatility from a floor — arithmetic the critic rightly called near-redundant — this fuses the intangible-heaviness penalty and the cash-generation requirement into a single interpretable return ratio, so the two archived channels interact multiplicatively inside one variable instead of through a MIN kink. It uses a three-year cash-flow average rather than a five-year floor, which roughly doubles coverage relative to the 0.091 leaders and lets us see whether a smooth, continuous specification can carry both a strong slope and a strong FF5 alpha.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( ratio( ma( oancf, 3 ), add( at, add( coalesce( gdwl, 0 ), coalesce( intan, 0 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Worst-Year Pre-Research Return on Penalized Capital
input_signals.hypothesis: Durable intangible productivity is the worst-year value of pre-research cash generation per dollar of acquisitiveness-penalized capital: a firm passes only if, even in its weakest year, the capital it truly deployed threw off enough cash to fund its own research program.
input_signals.reasoning: The archive shows two distinct strengths — MIN conjunctions with a five-year floor give strong Fama-MacBeth slopes (fmb 4.6–5.1) while smooth continuous ratios give the strongest FF5 alphas (ls_talpha up to 4.5 with fmb only 1.7) — and this fuses both properties into one variable by taking the floor *inside* the continuous ratio rather than conjoining two ranked legs. If it delivers a high slope and a high alpha simultaneously it is the natural consolidation candidate for the final generations.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( ts_min( ratio( add( oancf, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), add( at, add( coalesce( gdwl, 0 ), coalesce( intan, 0 ) ) ) ), 5 ) )

input_signals.name: Buying Innovation Instead of Building It
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(SUB(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), COALESCE(intan, 0)), 1), at), RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at))), IND_RANK(NEG(TS_MIN(RATIO(oancf, at), 5))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms that acquire their intangible capital instead of developing it — annual additions to booked intangibles exceeding annual research spending — are substituting deal-making for innovation, and when they also lack a cash-flow floor they are the population most exposed to integration failure and impairment.
input_signals.reasoning: The two intangible investment channels are compared here as same-unit annual flows, which is a construct the archive has never formed: prior work netted a five-year R&D stock against a booked intangible stock, mixing accumulation horizons. Conjoining the buy-over-build flow with a weak cash floor isolates the specific quadrant where the impairment mechanism should operate, giving a well-populated short leg without relying on subsample restatements of a profitability sort.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( sub( ratio( delta( add( coalesce( gdwl, 0 ), coalesce( intan, 0 ) ), 1 ), at ), ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), at ) ) ), ind_rank( neg( ts_min( ratio( oancf, at ), 5 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Income-Statement Cash Floor Behind Intangible-Light Firms
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), COALESCE(intan, 0)), at))), IND_RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(ADD(ib, dp), at), 5)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The economically relevant floor is cash earnings — income before extraordinary items plus depreciation and amortisation — which is measurable for the full history of the sample, so the intangible-light durability result should hold on the much larger population for which a statement-of-cash-flows series does not exist.
input_signals.reasoning: Every high-alpha archived conjunction is stuck at coverage 0.08–0.09 because it requires five years of oancf, and we cannot tell whether the effect is a genuine broad-sample regularity or an artefact of the post-1988 cash-flow-reporting era. Substituting the income-statement cash-earnings proxy is a measurement change, not a mechanism change, and a comparable alpha at roughly 0.146 coverage would make the final consolidated signal far more robust.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( neg( ratio( add( coalesce( gdwl, 0 ), coalesce( intan, 0 ) ), at ) ) ), ind_rank( ts_min( ratio( add( ib, dp ), at ), 5 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Recent Deal Flow Versus Legacy Intangible Stock
input_signals.hypothesis: The penalty attached to purchased intangibles reflects recent acquisitive behaviour — deals still facing integration and impairment risk — rather than a legacy intangible balance accumulated long ago and already validated by years of operations.
input_signals.reasoning: Every archived intangibles leg penalises the *stock* of goodwill and other intangibles, which conflates a 1998 acquisition with a 2019 one, whereas the five-year sum of additions isolates the live deal pipeline; holding the cash-flow floor fixed makes this a clean decomposition of the archive's most reliable intangibles leg. The answer determines whether the final signal should be built on a stock penalty or a flow penalty, which also matters for turnover since the flow measure decays naturally as deals age.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( neg( ratio( ts_sum( delta( add( coalesce( gdwl, 0 ), coalesce( intan, 0 ) ), 1 ), 5 ), at ) ) ), ind_rank( ts_min( ratio( oancf, at ), 5 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash Gross Profit Per Dollar of Knowledge-Augmented Capital
input_signals.hypothesis: Durable intangible productivity is literally output per unit of the capital that produced it: gross profit net of capital consumption, measured against a capital base that includes the firm's self-built knowledge stock alongside its recorded assets, so a firm scores high only if its research has translated into product-market surplus rather than into an expanding expense line.
input_signals.reasoning: This drops the cash-flow numerator that made the previous version a relabelled cash-based operating profitability and instead places the intangible capital where it belongs — in the denominator as productive capital — so the score falls, not rises, for firms that spend heavily on research without converting it into margin. The gen-0 attempt at this concept failed only because it used a five-year trend on a degenerate R&D-only denominator (coverage 0.060); the level form with an assets-plus-knowledge base is well conditioned for every firm and should run near 0.14 coverage.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( ratio( sub( sub( revt, cogs ), dp ), add( at, ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Research Funded Without Equity Dilution
input_signals.hypothesis: Research programs financed by repeatedly issuing equity transfer value away from existing holders and signal that internal economics do not support the program, whereas the same research intensity sustained without dilution reflects a self-financing innovator; the difference in book equity growth not explained by retained earnings is the dilution channel.
input_signals.reasoning: Replacing the flagged operator sweep, this introduces the one financing dimension the archive has never touched — external equity — after cash flow, working capital, total leverage and debt maturity have all been tested, and it is measured as a five-year cumulative issuance rate so it captures a financing regime rather than a single-year event. The interaction is essential: dilution is uninformative for firms with no research program to finance, and research intensity is uninformative without knowing who paid for it.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ), at ) ), ind_rank( neg( ts_sum( ratio( sub( delta( ceq, 1 ), delta( re, 1 ) ), at ), 5 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Net Durable Intangible Capital Behind a Cash-Earnings Floor
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), ADD(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), ADD(COALESCE(intan, 0), dlc))), at)), IND_RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(ADD(ib, dp), at), 5)))
input_signals.hypothesis: A firm's net durable intangible capital — knowledge built, less premium purchased, less debt falling due — is only credible when cash earnings never collapsed in the past five years, and both components can be measured from the income statement and balance sheet for the full sample.
input_signals.reasoning: Net Durable Intangible Capital produced the archive's highest FF5 t-statistic (ls_talpha 4.51, alpha 4.8%) at coverage 0.145 but an almost flat cross-sectional slope (1.69), while the cash-earnings floor produced a solid slope (2.93) with alpha 3.8% at the same coverage; the joint construct targets the missing dimension of each without reverting to the coverage-limited oancf history. This is the batch's leading candidate for a final signal that is simultaneously broad, precise in alpha, and monotone in the cross-section.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( sub( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ), add( coalesce( gdwl, 0 ), add( coalesce( intan, 0 ), dlc ) ) ), at ) ), ind_rank( ts_min( ratio( add( ib, dp ), at ), 5 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Same-Horizon Build Minus Buy with Cash Floor
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms should be judged on how they allocated intangible investment over a common horizon: five years of research spending against five years of additions to purchased intangibles, so a legacy goodwill balance inherited from the 1990s neither helps nor hurts, and only live allocation decisions count.
input_signals.reasoning: Gen 6 showed that the flow version of the intangibles penalty is as informative as the stock version (recent deal flow fmb 4.78 versus stock fmb 4.59) and that same-period buy-versus-build comparisons carry a strong negative slope (fmb −4.50), but the archived leader still nets a five-year research flow against a lifetime intangible stock — a horizon mismatch. Aligning both legs to five-year flows keeps the winning economics while removing a stale-balance-sheet component that should mechanically add noise and turnover.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( sub( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ), ts_sum( delta( add( coalesce( gdwl, 0 ), coalesce( intan, 0 ) ), 1 ), 5 ) ), at ) ), ind_rank( ts_min( ratio( oancf, at ), 5 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Worst-Year Productivity of Knowledge-Augmented Capital
input_signals.hypothesis: Durable intangible productivity means the capital base including self-built knowledge earned a solid product-market surplus even in its worst year; the level of that productivity is a cyclical reading, but its five-year floor identifies franchises whose knowledge capital genuinely works.
input_signals.reasoning: The level version of this productivity ratio delivered a respectable slope (fmb 3.47) but weak alpha (1.5%, ls_talpha 1.72), the mirror image of the continuous constructs whose alphas are strong and slopes weak, which suggests its top decile mixes genuinely productive franchises with firms enjoying a good year. Taking the floor inside the ratio — the transformation that lifted the penalized-capital construct to fmb 4.19 — tests whether downside durability is what converts a productivity measure into an alpha-bearing one, and it does so without adding a second ranked leg.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_rank( ts_min( ratio( sub( sub( revt, cogs ), dp ), add( at, ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ) ) ), 5 ) )

input_signals.name: Issuance Penalty Concentrated in Researchers
input_signals.hypothesis: External equity financing is not uniformly bad: issuing shares to fund a research program that the business cannot yet support is value-destroying, whereas the same issuance by a firm with no research program carries far less information, so the issuance penalty should be concentrated among research-intensive firms and reverse sign there.
input_signals.reasoning: The gen-6 dilution conjunction produced the archive's largest Fama-MacBeth slope (6.50) with no tradable alpha, which is what happens when a MIN kink places the informative firms in the middle of the score distribution rather than in the extreme deciles; the centered-gate structure instead puts self-funded researchers at one tail and dilutive researchers at the other, with non-researchers neutral, and that structure has repeatedly converted strong slopes into FF5 alpha in this archive. The proposal is a state-dependence test of a known effect rather than an additive blend of two anomalies, which is precisely the distinction the critic drew.

input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ), at ) ), sub( ind_rank( neg( ts_sum( ratio( sub( delta( ceq, 1 ), delta( re, 1 ) ), at ), 5 ) ) ), 0.5 ) )

input_signals.name: Acquisitive Expansion Without an Earnings Floor
input_signals.hypothesis: The clean short position is the firm that spent five years enlarging its purchased intangible base while never establishing a cash-earnings floor: the balance sheet grew in unverifiable assets exactly where operating performance failed to support them.
input_signals.reasoning: The archive's two best short-side results — the buy-versus-build conjunction (fmb −4.50, alpha −3.2%) and the impairment overhang (alpha −3.9%, ls_talpha −3.42) — each achieved only one of slope or alpha, and both were constrained either by the oancf history or by a one-sided kink. Pairing the five-year acquisitive flow with the negated income-statement floor gives a well-populated short leg at roughly 0.14 coverage and provides the short-side counterpart to Signal 1 for the final round.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( ts_sum( delta( add( coalesce( gdwl, 0 ), coalesce( intan, 0 ) ), 1 ), 5 ), at ) ), ind_rank( neg( ts_min( ratio( add( ib, dp ), at ), 5 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Never-Heavy Purchased Intangible Balance Sheet
input_signals.hypothesis: The current purchased-intangible balance is contaminated by survivorship: a firm that just impaired its goodwill looks intangible-light today precisely because the deal failed, so the honest measure is the worst (highest) intangible burden the firm carried over five years, and only firms that were never heavy deserve the credibility premium.
input_signals.reasoning: Every archived intangibles leg reads the current stock or the recent flow, both of which mechanically reward firms that wrote intangibles off, which is exactly the population the impairment story says should be penalised; the five-year maximum removes that contamination and is a new economic correction rather than a recombination. Pairing it with the income-statement cash-earnings floor keeps coverage near 0.14, and if the alpha rises relative to the current-stock version we learn the archive's leading result has been diluted by post-impairment firms sitting in the long leg.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( neg( ts_max( ratio( add( coalesce( gdwl, 0 ), coalesce( intan, 0 ) ), at ), 5 ) ) ), ind_rank( ts_min( ratio( add( ib, dp ), at ), 5 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Deal Premium in Years of Gross Profit
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), COALESCE(intan, 0)), MA(SUB(revt, cogs), 3)))), IND_RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(ADD(ib, dp), at), 5)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The payback horizon of a firm's purchased intangibles is best expressed in years of gross profit — the surplus actually available to recover a deal premium — and a premium that would take many years of gross profit to earn back is unrecoverable regardless of how small it looks against total assets.
input_signals.reasoning: This keeps the cash-denomination insight that produced the archive's best Sharpe (0.505) while replacing the fragile five-year cumulative operating cash flow denominator, which can be negative or near zero and would rank distressed cash-burners at the top, with gross profit, which is positive for virtually every operating firm and therefore monotone. Conjoining with the cash-earnings floor supplies the cross-sectional dispersion the standalone cash-denominated measure lacked (fmb −0.08) and holds coverage near 0.14 rather than the 0.09 of oancf-based versions.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( neg( ratio( add( coalesce( gdwl, 0 ), coalesce( intan, 0 ) ), ma( sub( revt, cogs ), 3 ) ) ) ), ind_rank( ts_min( ratio( add( ib, dp ), at ), 5 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Intangible Lightness with Stable Cash Margins
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), COALESCE(intan, 0)), at))), IND_RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(ADD(ib, dp), revt), 5))))
input_signals.hypothesis: The economic story specifies stable cash flows, and the right stability measure is the variability of the cash margin a firm earns on each dollar of revenue — a product-market property — rather than the variability of cash flow scaled by assets, which mixes margin stability with balance-sheet composition.
input_signals.reasoning: The asset-scaled volatility version worked (alpha 4.0%, fmb 3.28) but was restricted to coverage 0.081 by the oancf history, whereas the cash-margin version is computable from the income statement for the full sample and isolates operating predictability from leverage and asset intensity. It replaces an uninformative ablation with the one second-moment channel the archive has not tested, and it directly discriminates whether "stability" in the mandated story is a margin phenomenon or a balance-sheet phenomenon.

input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( neg( ratio( add( coalesce( gdwl, 0 ), coalesce( intan, 0 ) ), at ) ) ), ind_rank( neg( vol( ratio( add( ib, dp ), revt ), 5 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Worst-Year Return on Capital Charged for Deal Outlays
input_signals.expression: IND_RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(ADD(ADD(ib, dp), COALESCE(xrd, 0)), ADD(at, TS_SUM(DELTA(ADD(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), COALESCE(intan, 0)), 1), 5))), 5))
input_signals.hypothesis: A firm should be charged for the cash it actually committed to buying intangible capital during the measurement window, so the capital base is assets plus the five years of purchased-intangible additions, and the test is whether pre-research cash earnings cleared that base even in the worst year.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the arbitrary double-charging of the legacy intangible stock — inherited unexamined from the parent construct — with a principled charge equal to the deal outlays made inside the same five-year window over which the floor is computed, so numerator and denominator refer to one consistent period. It is a single-leg construct with no rank splice, buildable from the income statement and balance sheet at roughly 0.14 coverage, and it isolates whether the acquisitiveness penalty works through the capital base of a productivity ratio rather than as a separate ranked screen.

input_signals.name: Intangible Allocation Per Dollar of Business Scale
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), TS_SUM(DELTA(ADD(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), COALESCE(intan, 0)), 1), 5)), MA(revt, 3))), IND_RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(ADD(ib, dp), at), 5)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The build-versus-buy allocation should be judged against the size of the business it serves, not against the asset base, because asset scaling mechanically favours asset-light firms and conflates the intangible allocation decision with capital intensity.
input_signals.reasoning: Every intangibles leg in the archive is scaled by assets, so the recurring result could partly reflect an asset-light tilt rather than an allocation choice; revenue scaling breaks that link while leaving the economic content — five years of research spending net of five years of purchased-intangible additions — unchanged. Paired with the income-statement cash-earnings floor it also runs at roughly 0.13 coverage rather than 0.084, so a comparable alpha would show the effect is neither an asset-scaling artefact nor a post-1988 sample artefact.

input_signals.name: Profit-Funded Knowledge Stock
input_signals.hypothesis: Research dollars spent in profitable years are credible investment; research dollars spent in loss years are subsidised experimentation, so the priced knowledge stock is the cumulative research a firm financed while actually earning money, not its total research spending.
input_signals.reasoning: This puts the quality-intangibles interaction inside the accumulation itself — each year's research is admitted to the stock only if that year's earnings were positive — rather than conjoining a research measure with a separate profitability screen, which is a construction the archive has never used and which cannot be produced by ranking R&D intensity and profitability separately. It is a single continuous leg with no rank splice, computable for the full sample at roughly 0.145 coverage, and the smooth form is the one that has generated the archive's highest FF5 t-statistics.

input_signals.name: Build Minus Buy with Industry-Relative Earnings Floor
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), TS_SUM(DELTA(ADD(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), COALESCE(intan, 0)), 1), 5)), at)), IND_RANK(TS_MIN(IND_ADJ(RATIO(ADD(ib, dp), at)), 5)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The durability condition should be competitive rather than absolute: a firm qualifies if it out-earned its industry peers even in its worst year, which identifies a firm-specific moat supporting the research program rather than membership of a structurally profitable industry.
input_signals.reasoning: The industry-demeaned floor was tested only once, in gen 3, where it held up against the raw floor (fmb 4.24, alpha 3.8%, Sharpe 0.371) but was paired with a plain R&D-intensity leg and limited to the oancf sample; here it is combined with the strongest intangibles leg and the income-statement cash-earnings measure, extending it to roughly 0.13 coverage. This closes the run's central identification question — whether the repeated result is a moat effect or a residual industry-composition effect — while remaining a plausible top performer in its own right.

input_signals.hypothesis: The binding condition for a research program is not that cash flow was positive but that cash flow was large enough to pay the research bill in the worst year: a firm whose operating cash flow net of research spending never went negative has an unconditionally self-financing innovation program.
input_signals.reasoning: This is not a re-pairing of two archived legs because the quality gate itself now contains the intangibles variable — research spending is deducted from cash flow before the floor is taken — so the interaction operates inside both legs rather than only across them, and heavy researchers must clear a proportionately higher bar. The gen-2 attempt at self-funding used a count of qualifying years and failed on portfolio evidence (alpha −0.9%), whereas the magnitude form at the worst-year floor has never been tested and preserves the dispersion that a 0–5 count destroys.

input_signals.name: Profit-Funded Research Under an Acquisitiveness Constraint
input_signals.hypothesis: Two independent conditions define durable intangible productivity: research must have been financed out of profitable years, and the firm must not have been simultaneously buying intangible assets from outside; whichever condition binds determines the firm's credibility.
input_signals.reasoning: Replacing the unit-for-unit netting with a weakest-link conjunction removes the arbitrary weighting the critic identified, since neither channel is forced onto the other's dollar scale and each enters as a separate constraint. The profit-weighted accumulation is the genuinely new element — the earnings test is applied year by year inside the knowledge stock rather than as a separate screen — and pairing it with the validated five-year acquisitiveness penalty keeps coverage near 0.14 with no cash-flow-statement requirement.
